q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis

## (a) Time left until resolution
The question asks about NVIDIA's forward guidance to be released on August 26, 2026. Today is August 23, 2026, so **3 days remain** until the earnings release. This is extremely short timeframe — the guidance number is essentially already determined and will be announced in 72 hours.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The research provides explicit guidance that NVIDIA already issued for Q2 FY2027:
- **Guidance: $91.0 billion ± 2%**
- This creates a range of $89.2 billion (floor) to $92.8 billion (ceiling)
- Wall Street consensus is $91.9 billion

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will provide guidance at or very close to $91.0 billion. Companies typically announce their forward guidance once per quarter during earnings, and NVIDIA has already provided their Q2 FY2027 guidance in their Q1 earnings release (which occurred on May 20, 2026, based on the research).

The question asks "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?" This almost certainly refers to the forward guidance they will provide *during* the August 26 earnings call — which would be guidance for **Q3 FY2027**, not Q2.

However, re-reading the question more carefully, it specifically says "in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release" — this is asking about the earnings release event for Q2 results. During that event, they may:
1. Confirm or slightly adjust their previously-issued Q2 FY2027 guidance
2. Provide NEW guidance for Q3 FY2027

The ambiguity matters. But the research explicitly shows NVIDIA "Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2027" and provides "guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%."

Given that we're 3 days from the earnings release, the guidance for Q2 is almost certainly locked in at $91.0B ± 2%.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- A major chip supply shock or production issue
- Significant weakness in AI demand signals in the last weeks of Q1/early Q2
- Geopolitical escalation affecting China restrictions (though this is already priced into guidance)
- Unexpected customer cancellations or delays
- These would be highly unusual 3 days before earnings

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected demand in the final weeks of Q2
- Better-than-anticipated AI adoption/deployment
- Guidance could theoretically be raised slightly if conditions dramatically improved
- However, with 3 days to earnings, major upside revisions are unlikely

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides NVIDIA's actual Q2 FY2027 guidance: **$91.0 billion ± 2%**

This is not a forecast question — it's asking what a company will announce, and they have already announced it. The guidance range is $89.2B to $92.8B, with the midpoint at $91.0B.

---

## Conclusion

With only 3 days until the earnings release and NVIDIA having already provided their Q2 FY2027 guidance, this is extremely close to a known value. The guidance provided is $91.0 billion with a ±2% range.

The most likely scenario is NVIDIA reaffirms or slightly adjusts this guidance during the August 26 earnings call. The distribution should be heavily concentrated around $91.0B, with the ±2% uncertainty band representing the legitimate bounds.

Given the extremely short timeframe and that guidance is already publicly provided, I'm centering my estimate at the midpoint of their guidance range with minimal distribution around it.

Low (10th percentile): 89800000000
Median (50th percentile): 91000000000
High (90th percentile): 92500000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is scheduled to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings report on August 26, 2026, after the market closes [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8).

For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion, an 85% increase year-over-year and 20% sequentially, with Data Center revenue reaching $75.2 billion, up 92% year-over-year [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/) [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm).

NVIDIA's guidance for Q2 FY2027 revenue is $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/) [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This outlook explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China, a stance continued from the previous year [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, according to Yahoo! Finance, have an average revenue estimate of $91.9 billion for Q2 FY2027 [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). CNBC noted that NVIDIA's $91 billion guidance was well above the LSEG average estimate of $86.84 billion at the time of the Q1 earnings release [cnbc.com](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/05/20/nvidia-nvda-earnings-report-q1-2027.html). The company's guidance range for Q2 FY2027 places the ceiling near $92.8 billion and the floor near $89.2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).
